name: christianity
followers: about 2.4 billion, the largest religion in the world
founder: jesus of nazareth, and his apostles
scriptures: the bible: the old testament (the hebrew bible) and the new testament
places: jerusalem, bethlehem, rome, and many shrines of saints
summary: faith in jesus of nazareth as the son of god and savior, who died on the cross and rose from the dead. it began as a movement within judaism and became the religion of the roman empire and then of much of the world.
creation: the same account as the hebrew bible: god made the world in six days and made humans in his image. the gospel of john adds that all things were made through the word, which christians identify with jesus.
age: the bible gives no date. in 1650 archbishop james ussher added up its lifespans and got 4004 bce, a reckoning that was widely printed. most churches today accept the scientific age of the earth; some christians hold to a young earth.

events.text: god creates the world in six days and makes humans in his image, as told in genesis. the date is archbishop ussher's calculation of 1650, not a teaching of the church
adam and eve disobey god in the garden of eden; sin and death enter the world, and god promises that evil will one day be defeated
the story of israel, from abraham and moses to david and the prophets, which christians read as preparing the way for the messiah
the angel gabriel tells mary she will bear the son of god. jesus is born in bethlehem; angels sing to shepherds and wise men follow a star
jesus of nazareth is born, probably shortly before the death of king herod in 4 bce; the monk who later fixed the year 1 was a few years out
john the baptist baptizes jesus in the jordan. jesus begins teaching, healing the sick, and calls twelve disciples
jesus is crucified in jerusalem under the roman governor pontius pilate, an event also recorded by the roman historian tacitus
jesus rises from the dead, appears to mary magdalene and the disciples, and forty days later ascends into heaven
the holy spirit comes down on the apostles in jerusalem, and they begin preaching; christians see this as the birth of the church
paul, who had persecuted the first christians, becomes one himself after a vision on the road to damascus
at a meeting in jerusalem, the apostles agree that gentiles who become christians need not follow the whole jewish law
paul writes letters to the churches he founded, the oldest christian writings to survive
the emperor nero blames christians for the great fire of rome; by tradition peter and paul are put to death there
the four gospels, of mark, matthew, luke, and john, are written
the great persecution under diocletian, the last and worst attempt by rome to wipe out christianity
constantine and licinius issue the edict of milan, making christianity legal
the council of nicaea agrees the nicene creed: the son is "of one being with the father"
christianity becomes the official religion of the roman empire
jerome finishes translating the bible into latin, the vulgate, used in the western church for a thousand years
augustine of hippo finishes the city of god, written after the sack of rome
benedict founds the monastery of monte cassino; his rule shapes western monks and nuns
the great schism divides the catholic west from the orthodox east
pope urban ii calls the first crusade
francis of assisi gathers his first followers, who live in poverty and preach
martin luther's 95 theses begin the protestant reformation
john calvin publishes the institutes of the christian religion in geneva
the pope approves the jesuits, founded by ignatius of loyola; they soon run schools and missions worldwide
the council of trent leads the catholic counter-reformation
the king james bible is published in english
john wesley's conversion begins the methodist revival in britain and america
the second vatican council modernizes the catholic church; mass is now said in local languages
most christians now live in africa, latin america, and asia, not in europe and north america
christ will come again in glory; the dead will rise, the world will be judged, and god will make a new heaven and a new earth

people.name: mary
people.about: honored by most christians as the mother of god and by catholics and orthodox as queen of heaven

people.name: john the baptist
people.about: baptized jesus in the jordan; beheaded by herod antipas, as the historian josephus also records

people.name: jesus of nazareth
people.role: teacher from galilee, whom christians worship as the son of god
people.about: preached the coming of the kingdom of god, was crucified in jerusalem, and, christians believe, rose from the dead

people.name: mary magdalene
people.about: the gospels say she was the first to see the risen jesus

people.name: peter
people.about: a fisherman from galilee; catholics see him as the first pope, and by tradition he was crucified in rome

people.name: paul of tarsus
people.about: spread christianity across the eastern mediterranean; his letters make up much of the new testament

people.name: constantine
people.about: the first christian emperor; he called the council of nicaea

people.name: jerome
people.about: translated the bible into latin, the vulgate

people.name: augustine of hippo
people.about: his confessions and city of god shaped western christian thought more than any writer after paul

people.name: benedict of nursia
people.about: wrote the rule of saint benedict, the guide for most western monasteries

people.name: francis of assisi
people.about: gave up his wealth to live in poverty and serve the poor; loved all creatures as his brothers and sisters

people.name: thomas aquinas
people.about: joined christian teaching with the philosophy of aristotle in his summa theologiae

people.name: martin luther
people.about: taught that people are saved by faith alone and translated the bible into german

people.name: ignatius of loyola
people.about: founded the jesuits and wrote the spiritual exercises

people.name: john calvin
people.about: his teaching shaped the reformed and presbyterian churches

people.name: john wesley
people.about: rode some 400,000 kilometers preaching in the open air; founder of methodism

people.name: mother teresa
people.about: cared for the dying poor of kolkata and founded the missionaries of charity

people.name: martin luther king jr.
people.role: baptist minister and civil rights leader
people.about: drew on the bible and the example of jesus to lead non-violent protest against segregation

people.name: desmond tutu
people.about: fought apartheid without violence and chaired south africa's truth and reconciliation commission

glossary.definition: "one who is sent": the twelve closest followers of jesus, and early missionaries like paul.
the washing with water by which a person becomes a christian.
the christian scriptures: the old testament, shared with judaism, and the new testament, about jesus and the early church.
"universal": the church led by the pope in rome, the largest christian church.
the feast of the birth of jesus, on 25 december (7 january in many orthodox churches).
a short statement of belief, like the nicene creed of 325.
the feast of the resurrection of jesus, the most important day of the christian year.
holy communion or the mass: sharing bread and wine as jesus did at the last supper.
"good news": the message of jesus, and the four books of matthew, mark, luke, and john that tell his life.
the belief that god became a human being in jesus.
a community of monks or nuns living under a rule of prayer and work.
the eastern churches, such as the greek and russian, which split from rome in 1054.
the feast fifty days after easter, remembering the holy spirit coming down on the apostles.
the bishop of rome and head of the catholic church, seen as the successor of peter.
the churches that came out of the reformation, such as lutheran, reformed, anglican, baptist, and methodist, and later pentecostal.
jesus rising from the dead on the third day after his crucifixion; also the rising of all the dead at the end of time.
a holy rite through which, christians believe, god gives grace, such as baptism and the eucharist.
a holy person; in the catholic and orthodox churches, someone officially recognized as being in heaven.
the belief that the one god is three persons: father, son, and holy spirit.
